title: From Zero to Hero
subtitle: Grow up in Hearthcross. Become the adventurer your choices create.

rules.note: Developmental checks use normal 5E total-vs-DC success/failure. From Zero to Hero then applies its house-rule growth result: success earns flexible development, failure earns an off-path Lesson Point, natural-20 critical success earns one extra flexible point, and natural-1 critical failure can redirect one already-invested point from the attempted ability into the lesson ability.

start.possessions: Ordinary clothing and household items justified by family/home. No adventuring package.

development.spendTiming: between resolved growth beats and before graduation
development.lessonRule: A Lesson Point is locked to an ability different from the attempted ability and chosen because the failed scene plausibly taught that lesson.
development.criticalFailureRule: In addition to its Lesson Point, move one already-invested Development Point from the attempted ability into the same lesson ability when possible. This can lower one ability and raise another, but never reduces total earned development or the 27-point graduation floor.
development.criticalSuccessBonusRule: Critical success earns one extra flexible Development Point. Bonus development may raise the final base array above the guaranteed 27-point floor, but never above the absolute 30-point cap.

abilityGuide.DEX: Balance, sneak, climb, aim, or use precise hands.
abilityGuide.CON: Endure, protect through stamina, resist hardship.
abilityGuide.INT: Study, reason, engineer, recall, or solve.
abilityGuide.WIS: Notice, judge, empathize, track, or survive.
abilityGuide.CHA: Persuade, inspire, deceive, perform, or lead.

development.maturitySettlementRule: After all 21 base Development Opportunities are resolved, any stranded Lesson Points blocked by the 15 cap and any stranded partial invested progress that has not completed an ability increase may be converted into Flexible Maturity Points. Graduation is blocked until the pre-origin array has at least 27 point-buy value. Critical failures may redirect where development lands, but can never reduce the 27-point minimum.

challengeProfile.intent: Base success should be uncommon. Character-grounded play earns Advantage and meaningfully improves the odds.
criteria: Use an established bond, fear, value, aspiration, relationship, mentor lesson, familiarity, possession, or prior consequence in a way that materially fits the attempt.
Use a concrete feature of the scene or accept a meaningful cost/risk that makes the approach more credible.
Explain what the character actually does in the fiction; performance, accents, or eloquence are never required.
challengeProfile.restriction: The same generic justification cannot be repeated indefinitely. The advantage must be specific to the current scene and character history.
challengeProfile.resolution: With Advantage, roll two d20s and use the higher result. The kept die is the natural result used for the Level-0 critical-success/critical-failure tier.

development.statGrowthCapRule: The Level-0 base ability array may never exceed a point-buy value of 30. Development Points can continue to be earned after the cap, but they cannot be converted into additional ability-score power.

village.name: Hearthcross
village.pitch: A river-crossing village built around an old black standing stone, a market square, two mills, and a road that carries more strangers every year.
changesOverTime: Businesses open, close, or change hands.
Mentors age and their responsibilities shift.
Rivals can become friends, enemies, lovers, or leave town.
Locations damaged or saved in earlier chapters stay changed.
The old Watchstone mystery becomes more visible each year.

locations.name: Crossmarket
locations.use: festivals, contests, trade, public arguments and emergencies

locations.name: The Common Green
locations.use: games, training, militia drills and community meetings

locations.name: Shrine of the Open Hand
locations.use: faith, healing, charity and moral choices

locations.name: Quill House
locations.use: letters, records, lessons and arcane study

locations.name: The Hearth River
locations.use: fishing, ferrying, floods, rescues and travel

locations.name: Alderwood
locations.use: hunting, animals, survival and hidden paths

locations.name: The Watchstone
locations.use: old village landmark; warm to the touch before major storms

npcs.name: Captain Orren Vale
npcs.appearance: Broad-shouldered, iron-gray hair, left knee stiff in cold weather.
npcs.voice: Short sentences; asks questions instead of giving speeches.
npcs.wants: Hearthcross able to defend itself without becoming cruel.
npcs.fears: Training another young person who dies for his mistakes.
npcs.secret: He knows the Watchstone once reacted to bloodshed on the old road.
npcs.change: Strong at age 12; hand tremor appears by age 16; fully retired by age 18.

npcs.name: Sera Quill
npcs.appearance: Ink-stained fingers, copper spectacles, sleeves always rolled.
npcs.wants: Preserve the village records and understand the Watchstone.
npcs.fears: Her curiosity will expose something the village cannot contain.
npcs.secret: She has copied fragments of a pre-village ward diagram.
npcs.change: Local clerk at age 12; recognized scholar by age 18.

npcs.name: Sister Elwen Marr
npcs.appearance: Weathered face, shaved temple, patched blue shawl.
npcs.voice: Gentle until someone uses faith as an excuse for cruelty.
npcs.wants: Keep the village generous when fear rises.
npcs.fears: The shrine becoming a weapon in local politics.
npcs.secret: She once heard a voice beneath the Watchstone during a vigil.
npcs.change: Takes on two young acolytes as the party ages.

npcs.name: Bram Alder
npcs.appearance: Lean, sun-browned, one sleeve usually dotted with beeswax.
npcs.voice: Long pauses; describes people the way he describes weather.
npcs.wants: Keep Alderwood healthy and the river clean.
npcs.fears: The road expansion will ruin the woods.
npcs.secret: Animals avoid a buried stone circle north of town.
npcs.change: Becomes increasingly protective of the woods as traffic grows.

npcs.name: Tavi Brindle
npcs.appearance: Small, immaculate coat, brass key-ring at the hip.
npcs.voice: Warm salesman's cadence; notices every missing detail.
npcs.wants: Build Hearthcross into a prosperous stop without losing its character.
npcs.fears: Being remembered as merely a shopkeeper.
npcs.secret: Sometimes opens sealed letters for the reeve.
npcs.change: Expands from stall to storefront by age 16.

npcs.name: Maela Venn
npcs.appearance: Dark curls tied with green cord, sharp herbal smell on her apron.
npcs.voice: Dry humor; gives instructions while moving.
npcs.wants: Train enough hands that emergencies do not depend on her alone.
npcs.fears: A winter sickness she cannot treat.
npcs.secret: Keeps notes on strange fevers that coincide with Watchstone heat.
npcs.change: Takes over the full shop after her aunt retires.

npcs.name: Wren Cask
npcs.appearance: Heavy leather apron, burn scar across one forearm.
npcs.voice: Laughs loudly; criticizes work, not people.
npcs.wants: Leave the village safer than she found it.
npcs.fears: A bridge or building failing because she cut a corner.
npcs.secret: The Watchstone rings faintly when struck with her oldest hammer.
npcs.change: Becomes head of major village works by age 17.

npcs.name: Reeve Corlan Pike
npcs.appearance: Tall, neat beard, spotless boots even in mud.
npcs.voice: Formal in public; exhausted in private.
npcs.wants: Order, trade and a good reputation with the district.
npcs.fears: A disaster that proves he was unprepared.
npcs.secret: He suppresses old reports of the Watchstone to avoid panic.
npcs.change: Can become trusted ally or entrenched opponent based on player choices.

npcs.name: Jory Fen
npcs.appearance: Round face, quick hands, silver tooth.
npcs.voice: Every sentence sounds like the start of a story.
npcs.wants: A full common room and no blood on the floor.
npcs.secret: Keeps a coded ledger of travelers who ask about the Watchstone.
npcs.change: His daughter begins managing the inn by the final chapter.

npcs.name: Kess Reed
npcs.appearance: Freckled, cropped hair, always one scraped knuckle.
npcs.wants: To be first at something that matters.
npcs.fears: Everyone leaving Hearthcross before she can prove herself.
npcs.secret: Her older brother is tied to petty smugglers.
npcs.change: Can join the militia, leave with traders, or become a local organizer.

npcs.name: Nima Bell
npcs.appearance: Long braids, bright scarf, notebook of sketches.
npcs.voice: Asks the question everyone else avoids.
npcs.wants: See the world and draw places no one in Hearthcross has seen.
npcs.secret: She has sketched symbols near the Watchstone that change after storms.
npcs.change: May leave for a season and return with outside knowledge.

npcs.name: Rusk Thorn
npcs.appearance: Thin grin, oversized coat, silver ring he claims he won.
npcs.voice: Makes bad ideas sound like favors.
npcs.wants: Money and respect without waiting for either.
npcs.secret: Runs errands for smugglers by age 15.
npcs.change: Can become criminal, informant, or redeemed ally.

npcs.name: Old Sable
npcs.appearance: White hair, traveling cloak patched with unfamiliar cloth, black walking staff.
npcs.voice: Soft and precise; rarely answers the first question directly.
npcs.wants: Observe whether Hearthcross remembers why the Watchstone was raised.
npcs.fears: The ward failing before anyone is ready.
npcs.secret: She is descended from one of the ward's original keepers.
npcs.change: Appears only some years; her identity becomes clearer over time.

npcs.name: Mara Hale
npcs.appearance: Flour on her sleeves, red kerchief, strong forearms.
npcs.voice: Direct, affectionate, impossible to distract when worried.
npcs.fears: Adventure taking them farther away than home can reach.
npcs.secret: She once planned to leave Hearthcross herself.
npcs.change: Treat as a template guardian; replace or personalize per PC.

chapters.title: Spring Chore Day
chapters.groupActivity: The children are assigned a shared list of spring jobs before the first heavy rain.
chapters.objective: Finish the village chore list, help each other, and decide whose needs matter when there is not enough time to do everything.
chapters.pressure: Three chore bells. When the third bell rings, the spring rain arrives and unfinished work becomes someone else's problem.

growthBeats.title: The job board
growthBeats.prompt: The group has a cart, a pile of tools, and too many jobs: stack firewood, scrub the shrine steps, mend a fence, haul flour, and deliver medicine. How do you make the morning work?

approaches.STR: Take the heaviest jobs and keep the work moving.
approaches.DEX: Handle the fiddly repairs, knots, latches, and quick deliveries.
approaches.CON: Keep working steadily while everyone else tires or complains.
approaches.INT: Sort the list by tools, route, and dependencies so the group wastes no time.
approaches.WIS: Notice which household actually needs help first and which jobs can wait.
approaches.CHA: Organize the group, trade favors, and get reluctant helpers moving.

outcomes.criticalSuccess: The group finishes ahead of the first bell and earns a small favor from one household.
outcomes.success: The first set of chores is finished cleanly.
outcomes.failure: The jobs get done, but something is late, messy, or has to be redone after lunch.
outcomes.criticalFailure: A mistake creates a new chore and an embarrassed argument, but an adult turns it into a lesson rather than a punishment.

growthBeats.title: Mara's escaped goat
growthBeats.prompt: While the group is repairing a side fence, Mara's stubborn goat Clover slips loose and heads straight for the apothecary garden.

approaches.STR: Block Clover's path and wrestle her away from the herbs.
approaches.DEX: Circle around quietly and catch the trailing rope without spooking her.
approaches.CON: Keep pace through mud, brambles, and several failed attempts until she tires.
approaches.INT: Work out why the gate failed and use the yard layout to funnel her back.
approaches.WIS: Read the goat's behavior and lure her toward something she actually wants.
approaches.CHA: Recruit neighbors or mimic Mara's feeding call to get Clover to follow.

outcomes.criticalSuccess: Clover is caught without damaging the garden, and Maela lets the group keep a useful bundle of harmless herbs.
outcomes.success: Clover is caught before real damage is done.
outcomes.failure: Clover is caught, but tramples seedlings or ruins part of the repaired fence.
outcomes.criticalFailure: Clover causes a spectacular mess and someone gets knocked into the mud; the group still catches her and now owes Maela a repair favor.

growthBeats.title: Rain before supper
growthBeats.prompt: The clouds break early. One final delivery of flour, medicine, and lamp oil still has to cross the village before the roads become mud.

approaches.STR: Carry the heaviest load so the cart can move faster.
approaches.DEX: Take a faster footpath and keep fragile parcels dry.
approaches.CON: Push through cold rain and fatigue without abandoning the route.
approaches.INT: Repack and reroute the deliveries so one trip reaches all three stops.
approaches.WIS: Judge which delivery is most urgent if the group cannot protect everything.
approaches.CHA: Convince shopkeepers and neighbors to form a quick relay.

outcomes.criticalSuccess: Everything arrives dry, and the group earns a reputation for being dependable.
outcomes.success: The deliveries arrive before the roads turn bad.
outcomes.failure: Everything arrives, but one parcel is wet, late, or damaged and must be replaced.
outcomes.criticalFailure: The cart gets stuck and the group finishes soaked and late; nobody loses what they truly need, but the children owe an extra day of work.

chapters.choice: When there is time for only one extra job, do you help family, a friend, a mentor, or the household that needs it most?
chapters.consequence: Creates the group's first shared reputation and establishes which adults begin trusting them with real responsibility.

chapters.title: The Spring Dance
chapters.groupActivity: The group helps prepare Hearthcross's spring dance, attends it together, and navigates the small disasters that matter enormously at thirteen.
chapters.objective: Get the hall ready, survive the social tangle, and help the dance end as a good memory instead of a village argument.
chapters.pressure: The musicians start at sunset. Once the final lantern is lit, unfinished preparations become part of the evening.

growthBeats.title: Before the music
growthBeats.prompt: The Fox & Ferry yard needs benches, ribbons, lanterns, food tables, a dance floor, and a hundred tiny fixes before sunset.

approaches.STR: Move benches, barrels, tables, and the heavy lantern poles into place.
approaches.DEX: Hang ribbons, string lanterns, tune small instruments, and fix delicate decorations.
approaches.CON: Work through heat and repetition while others drift off to socialize.
approaches.INT: Measure the floor, solve the seating problem, and keep the setup from blocking exits.
approaches.WIS: Notice what is missing, who is overwhelmed, and which small problem will become a big one later.
approaches.CHA: Coordinate helpers, smooth over complaints, and convince older youths to actually help.

outcomes.criticalSuccess: The yard looks unusually good and one adult publicly credits the group.
outcomes.success: The dance space is ready when the musicians arrive.
outcomes.failure: The dance opens on time, but a crooked banner, missing bench, or mismatched table becomes an ongoing joke.
outcomes.criticalFailure: A setup mistake causes a public scramble just as guests arrive; the group fixes it together while half the village watches.

growthBeats.title: The awkward middle
growthBeats.prompt: A friend is being left out, a rival is showing off, someone has been stood up, and a small argument is spreading through the edge of the dance.

approaches.STR: Step physically between people before shoving starts and redirect the energy into a game or contest.
approaches.DEX: Slip between groups, pass a note, recover a dropped keepsake, or quietly arrange a better seating/dance pairing.
approaches.CON: Stay with the embarrassed or upset person even when doing so means missing the fun yourself.
approaches.INT: Piece together what was actually said and expose the misunderstanding before it gets worse.
approaches.WIS: Read who is hurt, jealous, frightened, or pretending not to care.
approaches.CHA: Talk someone down, invite the excluded person in, make a joke, or persuade the rival to back off.

outcomes.criticalSuccess: The argument becomes a story everyone laughs about later, and one relationship improves sharply.
outcomes.success: The social problem settles without spoiling the evening.
outcomes.failure: The argument ends, but someone leaves hurt or a friendship becomes strained.
outcomes.criticalFailure: The scene becomes the dance's embarrassing moment of the year; the damage is social, not permanent, and it creates a memorable lesson.

growthBeats.title: Lanterns in the wind
growthBeats.prompt: A sudden gust knocks down part of the lantern line and threatens the food tables while the musicians keep playing.

approaches.STR: Catch or brace a falling pole before it hits the crowd.
approaches.DEX: Move through the dancers and retie the loose line before more lanterns fall.
approaches.CON: Hold a support in place until someone can secure it properly.
approaches.INT: Identify the failed knot/anchor and improvise a safer rigging pattern.
approaches.WIS: Spot where the next lantern will fall and clear people from the danger first.
approaches.CHA: Turn the scramble into an organized cleanup without killing the mood.

outcomes.criticalSuccess: The group fixes the problem so smoothly that the music never stops.
outcomes.success: The lanterns are secured and the dance continues.
outcomes.failure: Several lanterns break and part of the food is lost, but nobody is hurt.
outcomes.criticalFailure: The whole line comes down in a harmless but spectacular crash; the dance moves indoors and the story follows the group for years.

chapters.choice: Who do you spend the last song with—or do you skip it to help someone else?
chapters.consequence: Changes friendships, rivalries, crushes, and promises that can reappear in later years without locking any romance.

chapters.title: Harvest Fair & Team Games
chapters.groupActivity: The group enters Hearthcross's team games while also helping their households run stalls and animals.
chapters.objective: Compete without letting the contest matter more than the people around you.
chapters.pressure: Three fair bells: registration, championship round, and closing market.

growthBeats.title: Pick your event
growthBeats.prompt: The team can enter hauling, obstacle running, endurance, riddles, tracking, or performance events—but everyone has to contribute.

approaches.STR: Anchor the hauling or wrestling leg.
approaches.DEX: Take the balance, archery, or obstacle leg.
approaches.CON: Handle the distance run, cold-water carry, or endurance leg.
approaches.INT: Solve the riddle, repair, or planning leg.
approaches.WIS: Track the marked route, judge animals, or spot hidden targets.
approaches.CHA: Handle storytelling, music, debate, or rally the team between events.

outcomes.criticalSuccess: The team wins its heat and earns a direct shot at the final.
outcomes.success: The team advances or places respectably.
outcomes.failure: The team loses the heat but earns a second-chance event or useful favor.
outcomes.criticalFailure: The attempt goes memorably wrong, but the crowd cheers the recovery and the team still gets a consolation route into the day.

growthBeats.title: The stall rush
growthBeats.prompt: During the busiest hour, two family stalls are short-handed, a pie tray falls, and a merchant's mule refuses to move.

approaches.STR: Move crates, right the stall, or muscle the mule's cart out of the lane.
approaches.DEX: Catch falling goods, weave through the crowd, and make fast precise fixes.
approaches.CON: Work two stations back-to-back without slowing down.
approaches.INT: Reorganize inventory, prices, and traffic so the bottleneck clears.
approaches.WIS: Notice which problem will hurt a family most if ignored.
approaches.CHA: Call customers, negotiate swaps, or recruit temporary help.

outcomes.criticalSuccess: The rush turns into the best sales hour of the day and someone shares the credit with the group.
outcomes.success: The stalls survive the rush with little loss.
outcomes.failure: The stalls recover, but money, food, or pride is lost along the way.
outcomes.criticalFailure: A public mess costs a family part of the day's profit, but the group helps repair the damage before closing.

growthBeats.title: The final relay
growthBeats.prompt: The closing team relay mixes a sack carry, narrow beam, memory puzzle, animal gate, and crowd-facing finish.

approaches.STR: Take the carry and make up ground through force.
approaches.DEX: Take the beam or precision handoff.
approaches.CON: Take the longest leg and keep pace despite fatigue.
approaches.INT: Memorize and solve the sequence station.
approaches.WIS: Handle the animal gate and choose the safest shortcut.
approaches.CHA: Call the handoffs, steady a panicked teammate, and lead the finish.

outcomes.criticalSuccess: The team wins or ties for the fair's top honor and can choose what to do with the prize.
outcomes.success: The team finishes well enough to be proud of the day.
outcomes.failure: The team falls short but finishes together instead of blaming one member.
outcomes.criticalFailure: A mistake costs the placing in dramatic fashion; the lesson is whether the group turns on each other or laughs and carries on.

chapters.choice: If the group wins anything valuable, keep it, split it, give it to family, or donate it to a village need?
chapters.consequence: Establishes how the group handles rivalry, recognition, money, and each other's mistakes.

chapters.title: Apprentice Week
chapters.groupActivity: For one week, Hearthcross youths rotate through real adult work before choosing where they want deeper training.
chapters.objective: Try several kinds of work, complete a shared commission, and discover which adults or crafts feel worth returning to.
chapters.pressure: The commission must be finished by market morning or the village pays an outside crew.

growthBeats.title: Morning rotations
growthBeats.prompt: Each youth is sent to a different mentor for half a day, then the group compares what they learned.

approaches.STR: Work forge bellows, timber, hauling, or militia drills.
approaches.DEX: Practice fine tools, locks, stitching, bow work, or precise craft.
approaches.CON: Take the long repetitive jobs others abandon.
approaches.INT: Copy records, measure materials, solve a repair, or research an old method.
approaches.WIS: Treat patients, handle animals, gather herbs, or learn field signs.
approaches.CHA: Deal with customers, teach younger children, perform, or mediate a complaint.

outcomes.criticalSuccess: A mentor notices unusual promise and offers an extra lesson later.
outcomes.success: The rotation produces useful familiarity and a good day's work.
outcomes.failure: The work is completed badly enough to require correction, but the mentor explains what went wrong.
outcomes.criticalFailure: A costly or embarrassing mistake happens under supervision; the mentor makes the youth help repair it and remembers how they respond.

growthBeats.title: The crooked pavilion
growthBeats.prompt: The group's shared commission is repairing the market pavilion. Halfway through, they discover an older support was installed crooked years ago.

approaches.STR: Brace and realign the timber while others secure it.
approaches.DEX: Reach the awkward joint and make the precise correction.
approaches.CON: Stay under the brace doing exhausting steady work until the fix is safe.
approaches.INT: Recalculate the load and redesign the repair instead of copying the bad old work.
approaches.WIS: Notice signs that another beam is starting to fail too.
approaches.CHA: Get two arguing mentors to agree on one repair plan.

outcomes.criticalSuccess: The pavilion ends up stronger than the original and Wren lets the group sign the hidden repair beam.
outcomes.success: The pavilion is repaired safely before market day.
outcomes.failure: The repair works, but costs extra materials or another day's labor.
outcomes.criticalFailure: The first fix fails inspection and has to be stripped out; the group loses pride and time, not the commission.

growthBeats.title: A real customer
growthBeats.prompt: Before the week ends, a traveler needs urgent help: a broken cart, an injured hand, a lost document, and little money.

approaches.STR: Repair or lift the damaged cart enough to travel.
approaches.DEX: Make the precise repair or recover the dropped/lost item.
approaches.CON: Do the difficult labor without demanding the traveler pay more than they can afford.
approaches.INT: Work out a cheap substitute repair or reconstruct the missing document's route.
approaches.WIS: Notice the injury or hidden problem the traveler is minimizing.
approaches.CHA: Negotiate payment, charity, or a trade that feels fair to both sides.

outcomes.criticalSuccess: The traveler leaves genuinely helped and later becomes an outside contact.
outcomes.success: The customer gets what they need at a fair cost.
outcomes.failure: The immediate problem is solved, but the group or mentor absorbs a cost.
outcomes.criticalFailure: The first solution makes matters worse; under a mentor's eye the group repairs the mistake and learns what professional responsibility feels like.

chapters.choice: Which mentor, craft, duty, or kind of work do you want to keep pursuing—and which one did you learn is not for you?
chapters.consequence: Adds persistent familiarity and mentor history, but never grants automatic Level-1 proficiency.

chapters.title: The Road to Bellmere
chapters.groupActivity: The group is trusted to take a cart of goods and letters to the neighboring hamlet of Bellmere without an adult escort.
chapters.objective: Get there, handle one night away from home, complete the deliveries, and return with the cart and each other intact.
chapters.pressure: Bellmere's market closes at noon on the second day; missing it means sleeping away from home another night.

growthBeats.title: Packing the cart
growthBeats.prompt: Everyone has different ideas about what the cart needs, and there is more cargo than space.

approaches.STR: Load and secure the heaviest cargo.
approaches.DEX: Pack fragile items tightly and tie down awkward loads.
approaches.CON: Take responsibility for the physically miserable driving shift.
approaches.INT: Balance weight, route, food, spare parts, and delivery order.
approaches.WIS: Read the weather and animals before deciding what to leave behind.
approaches.CHA: Negotiate whose cargo gets priority and keep the group from starting the trip angry.

outcomes.criticalSuccess: The cart is balanced, nothing important is forgotten, and the group leaves early.
outcomes.success: The cart is packed well enough for the road.
outcomes.failure: Something useful is left behind or packed badly, creating inconvenience later.
outcomes.criticalFailure: The load shifts outside town and the group has to repack everything under humiliating observation from younger children.

growthBeats.title: Night at Alder Ford
growthBeats.prompt: High water makes the usual ford questionable, and darkness is less than an hour away.

approaches.STR: Move stones, brace the cart, or physically guide it through the safest line.
approaches.DEX: Scout the bank and find a narrow foot crossing for people or light cargo.
approaches.CON: Take the cold-water job or keep watch while exhausted.
approaches.INT: Estimate depth/current and improvise a safer crossing method.
approaches.WIS: Read weather, current, animal behavior, and signs of an older crossing.
approaches.CHA: Convince the group to accept a slower plan—or persuade a nearby farmer to let them use a private footbridge.

outcomes.criticalSuccess: The group crosses safely and still makes a comfortable camp before dark.
outcomes.success: The group gets across without serious trouble.
outcomes.failure: The crossing costs time, wet supplies, or a wheel repair.
outcomes.criticalFailure: The cart becomes stuck or damaged; the group camps there and solves the problem at first light instead of suffering a catastrophic loss.

growthBeats.title: Bellmere market
growthBeats.prompt: One recipient has moved, one merchant disputes the agreed price, and the market bell is already ringing.

approaches.STR: Handle the heavy unloading fast enough to create time for the missing delivery.
approaches.DEX: Move through unfamiliar streets quickly and track down the moved recipient.
approaches.CON: Keep working through the long day while everyone else is tired and hungry.
approaches.INT: Check receipts, addresses, and market rules to settle the dispute with facts.
approaches.WIS: Read which local actually knows where the recipient went and whether the merchant is bluffing.
approaches.CHA: Negotiate the price dispute and get useful directions without insulting anyone.

outcomes.criticalSuccess: Every delivery is completed and the group returns with a new outside contact or invitation.
outcomes.success: The business is finished in time to head home.
outcomes.failure: The deliveries are completed, but the group loses money, time, or comfort.
outcomes.criticalFailure: They miss the return window and must spend an unplanned second night away; nothing is ruined, but families worry and trust has to be repaired.

chapters.choice: On the road home, do you talk about leaving Hearthcross someday, staying, or not knowing yet?
chapters.consequence: Makes the outside world real and records each character's first serious thought about life beyond the village.

chapters.title: The Long Storm
chapters.groupActivity: A two-day spring storm overwhelms ordinary village preparations, and the youths are now old enough that adults rely on them.
chapters.objective: Protect people, animals, and homes while deciding what cannot be saved.
chapters.pressure: Storm Level 0–3 rises after each beat; the village cannot protect every location at once.

growthBeats.title: Before the river rises
growthBeats.prompt: The village has one hour to board windows, move livestock, fill sandbags, and check isolated homes.

approaches.STR: Lead the heavy boarding, hauling, and sandbag work.
approaches.DEX: Move quickly between rooftops, shutters, ropes, and narrow spaces.
approaches.CON: Take the longest continuous work detail without stopping.
approaches.INT: Prioritize tasks using the flood map and available labor.
approaches.WIS: Notice the house, animal pen, or drainage ditch everyone else forgot.
approaches.CHA: Organize work crews and convince stubborn residents to evacuate early.

outcomes.criticalSuccess: The village is unusually well prepared and one later storm consequence is softened.
outcomes.success: The most important preparations are complete before conditions worsen.
outcomes.failure: One location is underprepared and becomes a harder problem later.
outcomes.criticalFailure: A preparation goes wrong publicly and costs precious time, but the mistake reveals where help is needed most.

growthBeats.title: Someone is still out there
growthBeats.prompt: A cart horse returns without its driver while a family reports that an older relative never came home.

approaches.STR: Force through debris or carry someone who cannot walk.
approaches.DEX: Follow the quickest dangerous path and cross unstable ground.
approaches.CON: Push through cold, wind, and exhaustion to keep searching.
approaches.INT: Reconstruct likely routes from chores, timing, and road conditions.
approaches.WIS: Track signs through rain and decide which clue is fresh.
approaches.CHA: Coordinate searchers and keep frightened family members useful instead of panicked.

outcomes.criticalSuccess: The missing people are found quickly enough to save both them and valuable supplies.
outcomes.success: The missing person is found and brought home.
outcomes.failure: The rescue succeeds but someone is injured, equipment is lost, or another task is delayed.
outcomes.criticalFailure: The first search route is wrong; the group finds the person only after conditions worsen, leaving a lasting scar or relationship consequence.

growthBeats.title: One crew, two crises
growthBeats.prompt: The mill wall is failing while floodwater enters three homes. The group cannot personally do both jobs.

approaches.STR: Take the physically dangerous stabilization job.
approaches.DEX: Reach trapped residents through a route larger rescuers cannot use.
approaches.CON: Hold a failing position long enough for another crew to finish.
approaches.INT: Devise a temporary engineering solution that buys one side time.
approaches.WIS: Judge which crisis is about to become irreversible.
approaches.CHA: Split and direct volunteers so both problems get at least some response.

outcomes.criticalSuccess: The group finds a way to preserve both lives and most property.
outcomes.success: The people are safe and the chosen priority is preserved.
outcomes.failure: Everyone survives, but one important village asset is lost or badly damaged.
outcomes.criticalFailure: The wrong priority becomes obvious too late; people still survive through fail-forward rescue, but a major location changes permanently.

chapters.choice: When safety and livelihood conflict, what does the group choose to save first?
chapters.consequence: Creates the first genuinely adult consequence the group carries into the final year.

chapters.title: The Last Spring Dance
chapters.groupActivity: The same group that once scrambled through the dance at thirteen now helps run it. Some of them may leave Hearthcross afterward.
chapters.objective: Finish one last celebration together, settle unfinished relationships, and respond when the Watchstone finally forces the village to confront its oldest problem.
chapters.pressure: The dance lasts three songs after midnight. When the third ends, the Watchstone's fracture can no longer be ignored.

growthBeats.title: This time, you're in charge
growthBeats.prompt: The younger children are setting up badly in exactly the ways the group once did. Adults now expect the eighteen-year-olds to make the evening work.

approaches.STR: Take the heavy work and teach younger helpers safe technique.
approaches.DEX: Handle delicate setup while showing someone younger how to do it.
approaches.CON: Keep the crew moving through a long day without snapping at them.
approaches.INT: Plan the layout and fix old recurring problems before they happen.
approaches.WIS: Notice which younger child is being left out or overwhelmed.
approaches.CHA: Delegate, encourage, and resolve complaints without doing every job yourself.

outcomes.criticalSuccess: The setup runs so well that younger children start copying the group's habits.
outcomes.success: The dance opens smoothly and on time.
outcomes.failure: The dance opens with a few problems the group must quietly manage.
outcomes.criticalFailure: A familiar old mistake returns in a new form; the group must decide whether to blame the younger kids or teach them better.

growthBeats.title: The last song before midnight
growthBeats.prompt: Old promises, rivalries, friendships, family expectations, and choices about leaving Hearthcross all come to the surface.

approaches.STR: Help with a physical task beside someone you need to talk to, letting the conversation happen while working.
approaches.DEX: Find the right private moment or recover an object tied to an old memory.
approaches.CON: Stay present through an uncomfortable conversation instead of walking away.
approaches.INT: Use what you know of the past six years to challenge a false assumption or old story.
approaches.WIS: Listen carefully enough to understand what someone is actually afraid of losing.
approaches.CHA: Say what needs saying: apologize, forgive, ask, refuse, promise, or say goodbye.

outcomes.criticalSuccess: A relationship reaches a clear, earned new state that can carry into adulthood.
outcomes.success: Something important is said or understood before midnight.
outcomes.failure: The conversation remains imperfect, but both sides know where they stand.
outcomes.criticalFailure: The attempt hurts before it helps; a hard truth comes out badly, yet the relationship is no longer built on avoidance.

growthBeats.title: When the Watchstone rings
growthBeats.prompt: At midnight the Watchstone cracks with a sound heard across Hearthcross. Old buried channels open under the green and the village must act immediately.

approaches.STR: Brace, lift, clear, or physically hold the failing structure long enough for others to work.
approaches.DEX: Cross unstable ground and place or retrieve the needed ward component.
approaches.CON: Remain at the dangerous job despite pain, fear, or exhaustion.
approaches.INT: Use Sera's records and six years of clues to understand what is failing.
approaches.WIS: Read the pattern of tremors, people, animals, and old signs to choose the safest response.
approaches.CHA: Unite mentors, rivals, officials, and frightened villagers behind one plan.

outcomes.criticalSuccess: The group resolves the immediate failure while preserving an extra relationship, location, or piece of the village's history.
outcomes.success: The group saves Hearthcross from the immediate crisis and earns the right to decide what comes next.
outcomes.failure: The village is saved with a permanent cost that becomes part of the characters' adult history.
outcomes.criticalFailure: The first plan fails dramatically, but six years of relationships provide a costly second route; Hearthcross survives changed, and the group graduates carrying that scar.

chapters.choice: After the dance and crisis, who stays, who leaves, who follows a mentor, and what promise keeps the group connected?
chapters.consequence: Freezes the village state, relationships, aspirations, and Level-0 history that carry into Level 1.

order: Freeze the earned Level-0 base array at 27–30 point-buy value.
Keep the already-locked 2014 race/species identity; do not reselect it.
Validate recorded innate race/species traits against the chosen 2014 source and activate any level-gated trait that is now legally available.
Apply the legal 2014 racial ability-score adjustment after the homebrew base array is frozen.
Choose and apply a legal 2014 background package.
Choose and apply a certified legal Level-1 class package, including HP/Hit Die, saves, proficiencies, equipment, and class features.
Carry childhood training only where a legal 2014 source grants the matching proficiency; otherwise keep it as history.
forbidden: 2024 origin feats unless an explicit separate house rule is enabled

order: Freeze the earned Level-0 base array at 27–30 point-buy value.
Keep the already-locked 2024 species identity; do not reselect it.
Validate recorded innate species traits against the chosen 2024 source and activate any level-gated trait that is now legally available.
Choose and apply a legal 2024 background, including its legal ability-score increase and Origin feat package after the homebrew base array is frozen.
Choose and apply a certified legal Level-1 class package, including HP/Hit Die, saves, proficiencies, equipment, and class features.
Carry childhood training only where a legal 2024 source grants the matching proficiency; otherwise keep it as history.

originLegacy.rawDefault: Narrative heirloom/contact only. No extra feat, ASI, proficiency, class feature, spell, or magic property.
originLegacy.heroicLegacyOptional: Optional house-rule campaign mode may add a bounded heirloom or other legacy after the GM explicitly enables it.
originLegacy.mentor: Persistent narrative contact; no automatic numerical bonus in RAW mode.

rawAudit.abilityArray: From Zero to Hero ability generation is a house rule. After all 21 base opportunities, the character is guaranteed a minimum base-array point-buy value of 27 and may never exceed a maximum value of 30, with no pre-origin score above 15.
rawAudit.proficiencies: Training/familiarity remains narrative until a legal 2014 race/background/class or 2024 species/background/class choice grants the proficiency.
rawAudit.heirloom: Heirloom remains mundane/narrative unless the selected ruleset or an explicitly enabled house rule grants a mechanical property.
rawAudit.mentor: Mentors are narrative contacts and grant no automatic numerical bonus unless an explicit house rule says otherwise.
rawAudit.mechanics: Race/species identity and target edition are locked before the first Growth Beat. The six-9 Level-0 array and 27–30 development envelope are homebrew. Once that array is frozen, all remaining background, class, proficiency, HP, spell, feat, equipment, deferred ability adjustment, and later advancement rules must follow the locked 2014 or 2024 ruleset exactly unless another homebrew is explicitly named.

lifeFirstDesign.principle: The early campaign is about growing up together, not being miniature adventurers.
lifeFirstDesign.escalation: Ages 12–15 center chores, dances, fairs, family, apprenticeships, friendships and small local problems. Age 16 expands the world. Age 17 introduces serious community danger. Age 18 combines a coming-of-age celebration with the final crisis/calling.
lifeFirstDesign.groupRule: Every chapter gives the whole group a shared reason to be together and multiple simultaneous jobs so each player can contribute without waiting for one protagonist.

growthBeatParticipation.rule: Each Growth Beat is one shared group situation. Every player character gets one Development Check inside that beat before the beat closes.
growthBeatParticipation.supportRule: A character may help another character fictionally, but still needs their own distinct contribution/check in the beat to receive that beat's Development Opportunity.
growthBeatParticipation.reframingRule: After each character acts, update the fiction. Later characters solve the new state of the problem rather than repeating an identical check.

prompts: What will your character still remember from this year?
Which relationship changed most for your character?
Is your character still striving to become the same thing? If not, what changed?
What changed in Hearthcross that your character notices?
yearbook.advantageLink: A recorded Yearbook memory may later justify Character Advantage only when it specifically matters to the current scene.

betweenYears.title: First Snow
betweenYears.prompt: The first snow keeps most of Hearthcross close to home. Choose one small memory: help family prepare for winter, spend a day with friends, visit a mentor, make or repair something, or get into harmless trouble.
betweenYears.villageChange: The Common Green gets its first permanent youth notice board after the spring chore crews prove they can be trusted.

betweenYears.title: High Summer
betweenYears.prompt: A hot week slows the village down. Where does your group gather when nobody has assigned you a job: riverbank, inn loft, smithy shade, shrine steps, orchard wall, or somewhere you invented yourselves?
betweenYears.villageChange: The Spring Dance becomes a stronger village tradition, and younger children begin copying the group's games and fashions.

betweenYears.title: The Long Evenings
betweenYears.prompt: Harvest is over and evenings stretch longer. Pick one thing your character practices badly but keeps returning to, and one person who notices.
betweenYears.villageChange: Tavi Brindle expands from a market stall into a small storefront, changing the feel of Crossmarket.

betweenYears.title: Choosing Where to Spend Your Time
betweenYears.prompt: Adult work is starting to compete with childhood freedom. Which mentor, craft, household duty, friend, or private interest gets most of your spare time this year?
betweenYears.villageChange: Maela Venn takes over more of the apothecary as her aunt withdraws from daily work.

betweenYears.title: Letters from Beyond Hearthcross
betweenYears.prompt: The first trip away makes the world feel larger. Who keeps in touch with someone outside the village, who wants to leave someday, and who feels more certain Hearthcross is home?
betweenYears.villageChange: More travelers begin using Hearthcross as a stop between Bellmere and the district road; strangers become less unusual.

betweenYears.title: After the Storm
betweenYears.prompt: The village repairs what it can. What job does your character keep showing up for after nobody is asking anymore, and which adult starts treating them differently because of it?
betweenYears.villageChange: Captain Orren's age becomes harder to ignore; younger villagers begin taking over duties he once handled automatically.

villageTimeline.ambientChange: The youth notice board appears on the Common Green.
villageTimeline.choiceSensitive: Whichever household the group helped most starts treating them as dependable rather than merely children.

villageTimeline.ambientChange: The Spring Dance becomes an annual youth-led tradition.
villageTimeline.choiceSensitive: Friendships, rivalries, crushes, and embarrassments from the dance remain visible next year.

villageTimeline.ambientChange: Crossmarket grows busier as Tavi's storefront opens.
villageTimeline.choiceSensitive: How the group handled winning/losing affects local reputation.

villageTimeline.ambientChange: Several youths begin regular apprenticeships or household work.
villageTimeline.choiceSensitive: Mentors remember both good work and how mistakes were repaired.

villageTimeline.ambientChange: Outside travelers and letters become more common after the Bellmere road trip.
villageTimeline.choiceSensitive: The group gains or loses family trust depending on how responsibly they handled independence.

villageTimeline.ambientChange: Storm repairs permanently change at least one visible village location.
villageTimeline.choiceSensitive: Adults begin addressing the group as near-peers in emergencies.

villageTimeline.ambientChange: The village prepares for some of the group to leave and others to stay.
villageTimeline.choiceSensitive: The final crisis locks the Hearthcross state carried into Level 1.

graduationKeepsakes.certificateSubtitle: From Zero to Hero · Completion of the Level-0 Origin Years
graduationKeepsakes.certificateStatement: Recognizes the character's completed childhood origin campaign and readiness to begin certified Level-1 creation in the selected 2014 or 2024 ruleset.
graduationKeepsakes.ruleBoundary: The graduation keepsakes are commemorative only. They grant no feat, proficiency, ASI, spell, class feature, equipment entitlement, magic-item property, or other mechanical benefit.

competitionStandard.placementLabel: Always record official place and field size, such as 4th of 6.
competitionStandard.tieRule: Break ties first by the higher kept d20. If still tied for a podium place, make one story-only d20 tiebreak roll; no Development Point is awarded.
competitionStandard.criticalSuccessDecoration: A critical success may add a Legendary Finish badge to the card but grants no extra scrapbook mechanic.
competitionStandard.criticalFailureDecoration: A critical failure should prefer an event-specific mishap/consolation title when the character finishes outside the podium.
competitionStandard.noDevelopment: Competition placement itself grants no extra Development Points. The competition's Development Card carries only the growth result already produced by that character's Development Check.
competitionStandard.consolationAssignment: For 4th–6th place, use consolation entries in order: 4th gets #1, 5th gets #2, 6th gets #3, unless an event-specific place/field-size special award overrides it.
competitionStandard.cardBuildRule: Every competitor receives one scrapbook card. That same card is the Development Card for the competition Growth Beat when the competition is a Growth Beat. Podium/consolation title records placement; development fields record how the character actually grew from the check.

coreFairnessSlate.rule: The six core development competitions contain exactly one STR, DEX, CON, INT, WIS, and CHA contest. Because every Upbringing Lean has exactly 2 Favored, 2 Neutral, and 2 Challenging abilities, every profile experiences exactly 2 Favored, 2 Neutral, and 2 Challenging core competitions.
coreFairnessSlate.optionalSideContests: Optional extra contests may award scrapbook memories and placements but must not add Development Points unless they replace a declared Growth Beat under the same six-ability fairness audit.

competitionStandard.rankingRule: For a core competition, every contestant rolls the same primary ability. Use normal Upbringing Lean and Character Advantage cancellation. Rank by final check total, then kept d20, then a story-only d20 tiebreak. This keeps the contest comparable while preserving different childhood odds.
competitionStandard.threePlayerRule: With three players, add one NPC competitor (Fen Bell or Lark Cask, run by the DM) so podium places stay earned. The NPC gets no scrapbook card and no Development Point. Record field size as 4.

competitions.name: The Rat Race
competitions.prompt: A ridiculous looping dash around hay bales, market stalls, and painted wooden rats. Speed helps, but route-reading, endurance, and crowd sense can matter too.

1.title: Winner of the Rat Race
1.memory: Fastest through the fairground course when it counted.

2.title: Rat Race Runner-Up
2.memory: One turn, one stumble, or one breath away from first.

3.title: Third by a Tail
3.memory: Made the podium and will absolutely claim it was closer than it looked.

consolations.title: Lost a Shoe, Finished Anyway
consolations.memory: One shoe stayed behind. You did not.

consolations.title: Wrong Turn at the Turnip Stall
consolations.memory: For several seconds, you were winning a completely different race.

consolations.title: The Rat Was Faster
consolations.memory: You finished. The painted rat mascot somehow looked smug about it.

competitions.placementMethod: All contestants use the same primary ability. Rank by final check total; break ties by higher kept d20, then one story-only d20 tiebreak if needed. Placement itself adds no Development Points.

competitions.name: Pie-Eating Contest
competitions.prompt: No hands. Too much berry pie. An audience that gets louder as judgment gets worse.

1.title: Hearthcross Pie Champion
1.memory: A clean victory purchased at considerable personal dignity.

2.title: Second Helping
2.memory: Runner-up, with enough pie consumed to question every decision that led here.

3.title: Crust and Honor
3.memory: Third place, still upright, technically proud.

consolations.title: Face Full of Pie
consolations.memory: At some point the contest stopped being about winning and became about surviving the photograph.

consolations.title: Too Much, Too Fast
consolations.memory: An important lesson about enthusiasm, pacing, and berry filling.

consolations.title: Never Again (Until Next Year)
consolations.memory: A solemn promise made while covered in crumbs.

competitions.placementMethod: All contestants use the same primary ability. Rank by final check total; break ties by higher kept d20, then one story-only d20 tiebreak if needed. Placement itself adds no Development Points.

competitions.name: One-Legged Dash
competitions.prompt: Hop, wobble, shout, recover, and somehow cross the finish line while the village laughs with you.

1.title: One-Legged Dash Champion
1.memory: Balance, stubbornness, and a very tired hopping leg earned first place.

2.title: Silver Hop
2.memory: Second place and only slightly less graceful than the winner.

3.title: Bronze Knee
3.memory: Third place, a ribbon, and a new appreciation for having two legs.

consolations.title: Participation Ribbon, Earned the Hard Way
consolations.memory: You did not make the podium. You did make it to the finish.

consolations.title: Technically Finished
consolations.memory: The judges eventually agreed that your final movement counted as crossing the line.

consolations.title: 6th Place in a Five-Person Race
consolations.memory: The official result says fifth. The handmade consolation ribbon says sixth. Nobody will explain why.

5-of-5.title: 6th Place in a Five-Person Race
5-of-5.memory: Official result: fifth of five. The handmade consolation ribbon still says sixth. Nobody will explain why.

competitions.placementMethod: Optional side contest. Award placement/memory cards only; it is not one of the six fairness-core development contests.

competitions.name: Sack Haul
competitions.prompt: Move awkward grain sacks through a short obstacle lane without splitting them or yourself.

1.title: Strongest Back at the Fair
1.memory: First across with the sack intact.

3.title: Third and Still Carrying
3.memory: Podium finish with all the grain still inside the sack.

consolations.title: Carried the Wrong Sack
consolations.memory: Impressive effort. Wrong pile.

consolations.title: Grain Trail Award
consolations.memory: Your sack finished lighter than it started.

consolations.title: Most Determined Walk Home
consolations.memory: The race ended before your determination did.

competitions.placementMethod: All contestants use the same primary ability. Rank by final check total; break ties by higher kept d20, then one story-only d20 tiebreak if needed. Placement itself adds no Development Points.

competitions.name: Riddle Table
competitions.prompt: Three riddles, one trick question, and a judge who enjoys watching confident people realize they misunderstood the wording.

1.title: Sharpest Mind at the Table
1.memory: First to solve the final riddle without falling for the trick.

2.title: Almost Outsmarted the Judge
2.memory: Second place, which the judge insists is 'the first incorrect answer.'

3.title: Third Thought Was the Charm
3.memory: The answer arrived eventually, and in time for a ribbon.

consolations.title: Confidently Incorrect
consolations.memory: The answer was delivered beautifully. It was also wrong.

consolations.title: Solved the Wrong Riddle
consolations.memory: An excellent solution to a question nobody asked.

consolations.title: Participation Quill
consolations.memory: A tiny wooden quill awarded for refusing to leave the table.

competitions.placementMethod: All contestants use the same primary ability. Rank by final check total; break ties by higher kept d20, then one story-only d20 tiebreak if needed. Placement itself adds no Development Points.

competitions.name: Lantern Decorating Contest
competitions.prompt: Build, paint, fold, or decorate a spring lantern before the evening dance.

1.title: Best Spring Lantern
1.memory: The lantern everyone pointed out when the lights came on.

2.title: Second Brightest
2.memory: Beautiful enough to make first place nervous.

3.title: Third Light of Spring
3.memory: A podium ribbon and a lantern worth keeping.

consolations.title: Most Glue on One Person
consolations.memory: Some of the lantern survived too.

consolations.title: Abstract Lantern Award
consolations.memory: Nobody understood it. Several people claimed that was the point.

consolations.title: Still Lit at Midnight
consolations.memory: It did not win, but it outlasted several prettier lanterns.

competitions.placementMethod: All contestants use the same primary ability. Rank by final check total; break ties by higher kept d20, then one story-only d20 tiebreak if needed. Placement itself adds no Development Points.

competitions.name: Hearthcross Scavenger Hunt
competitions.prompt: Teams receive six ordinary village clues and must notice what everyone else walks past: tracks, weather signs, shop marks, animal behavior, and hidden landmarks.
competitions.placementMethod: All contestants use WIS. Rank by final check total; break ties by higher kept d20, then one story-only d20 tiebreak if needed. Placement itself adds no Development Points.

1.title: Eyes of Hearthcross
1.memory: You found the last clue before anyone else realized where to look.

2.title: Second to Notice
2.memory: One clue behind, and still seeing more than most people did.

3.title: Third Trail Home
3.memory: A podium finish built on patience and noticing the small things.

consolations.title: Followed the Wrong Goose
consolations.memory: The goose seemed extremely confident. The goose was not part of the contest.

consolations.title: Found Something Else Useful
consolations.memory: Not the clue, but still something nobody else noticed.

consolations.title: Participation Magnifying Glass
consolations.memory: A wooden lens frame awarded for refusing to stop looking.

scrapbook.rule: Every resolved Growth Beat creates exactly one Development Card for that character. The card records the actual development consequence already awarded by the growth system. Cards do not add extra Development Points beyond that result; they are the persistent source-of-truth explaining how the character was built.

outcomeMapping.failure: Card records +1 off-path Lesson Point in the chosen lesson ability.
outcomeMapping.criticalFailure: Card records +1 off-path Lesson Point and any 1-point invested-development redirection.

developmentCard.auditRule: The sum of Development Card effects must reconcile exactly with the character's Development wallet, invested development, critical bonus count, and hard-lesson redirects. Each card also records the Level-0 Upbringing Lean lane and effective roll mode that shaped the odds without changing the starting ability score.

yearbookCards.rule: Yearbook, bond, reputation, and pure memory cards may be added in addition to Development Cards, but they carry no Development Points unless they are also the card for a resolved Growth Beat.

upbringingLeans.fairnessRule: Every preset has exactly two advantaged abilities, two neutral abilities, and two disadvantaged abilities. No preset receives more favorable or unfavorable ability lanes than another.
upbringingLeans.interactionRule: Use standard 5E-style advantage/disadvantage cancellation. Any Advantage source plus any Disadvantage source resolves to a normal roll. Multiple Advantage sources never stack; multiple Disadvantage sources never stack.
upbringingLeans.characterAdvantageInteraction: Character Advantage can improve a neutral upbringing check to Advantage or cancel an upbringing Disadvantage to a normal roll. It cannot create double Advantage.
upbringingLeans.level1Boundary: Upbringing Lean changes only Level-0 developmental checks. It grants no Level-1 ability modifier, proficiency, feat, class feature, spell, save proficiency, or permanent Advantage/Disadvantage.

profiles.label: Barbarian-shaped upbringing
profiles.description: A childhood of heavy work, rough play, carrying, climbing, weather, and learning to endure before learning to analyze.

profiles.label: Bard-shaped upbringing
profiles.description: A childhood around performance, quick hands, social rooms, stories, music, errands, and reading an audience.

profiles.label: Cleric-shaped upbringing
profiles.description: A childhood of service, patient work, community responsibility, ritual, care, and learning to endure other people's needs.

profiles.label: Druid-shaped upbringing
profiles.description: A childhood outdoors with animals, weather, seasons, practical endurance, and learning to notice what the land is saying.

profiles.label: Fighter-shaped upbringing
profiles.description: A childhood of labor, drills, carrying, wrestling, repetitive practice, and being expected to stand your ground.

profiles.label: Monk-shaped upbringing
profiles.description: A childhood built around balance, discipline, observation, repetition, restraint, and precise physical practice.

profiles.label: Paladin-shaped upbringing
profiles.description: A childhood of duty, presence, physical training, public promises, responsibility, and being expected to act when others hesitate.

profiles.label: Ranger-shaped upbringing
profiles.description: A childhood of scouting, hunting, quick movement, watching trails, judging distance, and learning when not to be noticed.

profiles.label: Rogue-shaped upbringing
profiles.description: A childhood of quick hands, locks, routes, tricks, noticing mechanisms, and solving problems before stronger people notice them.

profiles.label: Sorcerer-shaped upbringing
profiles.description: A childhood of forceful personality, stubborn vitality, strange instincts, and learning to survive attention you did not always ask for.

profiles.label: Warlock-shaped upbringing
profiles.description: A childhood of forbidden books, bargains, secrets, persuasion, curiosity, and learning to get answers adults would rather hide.

profiles.label: Wizard-shaped upbringing
profiles.description: A childhood of study, memory, careful observation, puzzles, books, and thinking through problems before acting.

preClassShell.startingAbilityRule: All six Level-0 base ability scores begin at 9 regardless of race/species. This is an explicit house-rule override used only for the origin campaign.
preClassShell.editionRule: The target rules edition (2014 or 2024) locks with race/species before the first Growth Beat so the later RAW handoff has one authoritative rules source.
preClassShell.raceSpeciesRule: Race/species identity is chosen before play and cannot change during the origin campaign or at graduation.
preClassShell.intrinsicTraitRule: Source-verified race/species traits that are innate and not gated by class, proficiency bonus, or character level may be recorded as active Level-0 traits. The site stores user-entered notes rather than reproducing proprietary rules text.
preClassShell.gatedTraitRule: Any race/species trait whose source requires a character level, proficiency bonus, class feature, spellcasting feature, or other unavailable prerequisite remains recorded but dormant until that prerequisite legally exists.

abilityAdjustmentRule.2014: Any normal 2014 racial ability-score adjustment is deferred until after the homebrew Level-0 base array is frozen at graduation.
abilityAdjustmentRule.2024: Any normal 2024 background ability-score adjustment is deferred until after the homebrew Level-0 base array is frozen at graduation.

preClassShell.historyRule: Level-0 practice with skills, tools, weapons, languages, magic, crafts, medicine, and similar activities remains familiarity/history unless a legal Level-1 source grants the proficiency or feature.

rawPlaceholders.label: Subclass
rawPlaceholders.filledBy: only when the selected edition/class legally grants it

rawPlaceholders.label: HP / Hit Die
rawPlaceholders.filledBy: selected Level-1 class and legal rules

rawPlaceholders.label: Feat / Origin Feat
rawPlaceholders.filledBy: only if legally granted by the selected edition

rawPlaceholders.label: Edition Ability Adjustment
rawPlaceholders.filledBy: 2014 race or 2024 background after Level-0 array freeze

preClassShell.level1Rule: Anything not explicitly listed as a Level-0 homebrew field or immutable race/species identity must be filled from the selected edition's legal rules at graduation unless the table deliberately enables another named homebrew.
